stories.statLabel: buses and ambulances in the convoy
stories.headline: Civilians evacuated from besieged Oleshky in first joint relief mission
body: People in Russian-held Oleshky, across the Dnipro from Kherson, were evacuated on Friday in a joint relief operation.
It is the first of its kind in more than four and a half years of war.
A convoy of 25 buses and ambulances brought food and medicine for the few thousand people left, including about 50 children.
stories.vc: Humanitarian deals like this are tests for wider ceasefire talks, which markets watch for signs of a rebuilding boom.

stories.headline: Canada and the EU launch an 'Alliance for the Future'
body: Canada's Mark Carney and the EU's Ursula von der Leyen announced a new alliance at their summit in Montreal.
They call it a hedge against unpredictable geopolitics and a source of stability for citizens.
Other like-minded countries are invited to join.
stories.joke: Two friends start a club. Membership open, one neighbour pointedly not mentioned.
stories.vc: Deeper Canada–EU ties could redirect trade and investment away from the US, a shift India's exporters will watch.

stories.headline: Qatari mediators fly to Tehran to revive the US–Iran ceasefire
body: A Qatari delegation working with US officials arrived in Tehran on Friday to try to revive a ceasefire.
JD Vance's letter to Iran's security chief has reportedly been well received.
But Trump has told Gulf allies to prepare, and Pakistan's army says it is 'cautiously optimistic' on mediation.
stories.joke: Mixed signals so loud even the mediators need mediators.
stories.vc: Any ceasefire would ease oil and shipping costs through Hormuz, good news for India's fuel import bill.

stories.headline: India proposes a privacy-first way to share data for AI training
body: The IT ministry has proposed a consent-based framework, DEPA for AI training, to help build AI models on Indian data.
Companies could train models together without handing over the underlying data.
Trained models would need independent checks for bias, fairness, safety and explainability.
stories.joke: Finally, a plan to feed AI without feeding it your Aadhaar.
stories.vc: Access to large Indian datasets is the main edge local AI startups lack; this could lower that barrier.

stories.statLabel: labour laws merged into one code
stories.headline: India sets up a social security board for gig workers
body: The Labour Ministry has formed a National Social Security Board for unorganised, gig and platform workers.
It falls under the 2020 Code on Social Security, which merged nine labour laws.
Platforms, unions, worker groups and governments will all have seats, chaired by the Labour Minister.
stories.joke: Your delivery partner may finally get benefits faster than your order.
stories.vc: Welfare contributions could raise costs for Zomato, Swiggy, Uber and others, a key margin question for investors.

stories.headline: Karnataka plans to grow seven cities beyond Bengaluru
body: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar unveiled the Karnataka State Regional Urbanisation Plan 2047.
It names Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Belagavi, Kalaburagi, Ballari and Shivamogga as growth hubs.
The aim is to spread jobs and infrastructure so growth isn't only in Bengaluru.
stories.joke: Plan 2047: so Bengaluru traffic can finally get some company.
stories.vc: Tier-2 hubs with good infra could pull startups and offices out of Bengaluru, cutting costs for companies.

stories.headline: North Korea blamed for record $6.3B Binance crypto heist
body: Hackers linked to North Korea stole at least $6.3 billion from Binance, the biggest crypto theft on record.
About half has been frozen, and Binance says it will cover all user losses.
Binance says the attack began with a compromised engineer's laptop; most of it unfolded in about 20 minutes.
stories.joke: One laptop, 20 minutes, $6.3 billion. Worst IT ticket ever.
stories.vc: Hacks this big push regulators to tighten exchange security rules, raising costs across crypto platforms.

stories.headline: Investors get nervous about Big Tech's $740B AI spending
body: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft plan to spend over $740 billion this year, mostly on AI data centres and chips.
Investors now worry about negative cash flow, rising debt and whether it will pay off.
The Nasdaq fell 2.9% on Friday and chip stocks were hit hard.
stories.joke: Spending like there's no tomorrow, until tomorrow asks for returns.
stories.vc: If Big Tech slows AI spending, chipmakers and data-centre suppliers feel it first, including Indian IT and infra plays.

stories.headline: Intel crashes 28%, wiping $12B off the US government's stake
body: Intel's stock fell about 28% on Friday after a weak fourth-quarter forecast of $15–16 billion in revenue.
That cut the value of the US government's 10% stake by about $12 billion.
Even so, the stock is still up more than 70% this year.
stories.joke: The government bought the dip. Then the dip bought the government.
stories.vc: Government stakes in companies add political risk; a bad quarter now becomes a taxpayer headline.

stories.headline: Anthropic may get a 'junk' credit rating after its IPO, FT reports
body: Blackstone told investors it expects Anthropic to get a high 'junk' rating, in the double-B range, after its IPO.
It had earlier said Anthropic would get an investment-grade rating before 2027.
Blackstone anchored a recent $63 billion deal to finance Anthropic's chips.
stories.joke: Huge revenue, huge losses, and now a credit score like a college student's.
stories.vc: A junk rating means pricier borrowing for the chips AI labs need, a cost that eats into future profits.

image.credit: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: Waymo picks Toyota to build its robotaxis for Japan and the UK
body: Toyota will build 2027 bZ4X electric cars fitted with Waymo's self-driving system at its Takaoka factory.
Testing starts in Japan next year, where Waymo plans a robotaxi service.
The cars are meant for right-hand-drive markets like the UK, where Waymo already tests in London.
stories.joke: Japan gets robotaxis. Bengaluru gets a fourth flyover tender.
stories.vc: Pairing with big carmakers lets robotaxi firms scale without building factories, a model others will copy.

stories.headline: Two women battle to lead Los Angeles
body: Karen Bass, the first woman elected mayor of Los Angeles, is running for a second term.
Her challenger is council member Nithya Raman, a former ally who entered on the last day to register.
The race pits Bass's experience against Raman's promise of bigger change.
stories.joke: Whoever wins, LA's mayor is a woman. Patriarchy, please sit this one out.
stories.vc: LA's next mayor controls a huge budget for housing and homelessness, sectors that draw large public and private spending.

stories.headline: Muslim women lawmakers face a wave of online hate before the vote
body: Ohio lawmaker Munira Abdullahi, the state's first Muslim woman legislator, says this is the worst Islamophobia she has faced.
She says far-right activist Laura Loomer has posted about her nonstop, including AI-edited photos.
Muslim women in office say they want to be judged on their work, not their faith.
stories.vc: Online abuse pushes women out of public life; platforms face growing pressure to spend on moderation.

stories.headline: Man accused of secretly filming a woman on Namma Metro questioned
body: Bengaluru police questioned a 38-year-old man accused of secretly filming a woman passenger on the Metro.
His phone has been seized for forensic checks; he denies it.
The alleged filming happened near Pattandur Agrahara station; he has anticipatory bail but must cooperate.
stories.vc: Women's safety on public transport shapes how many women can commute to work, and so their job options.

stories.headline: Fortis buys Bengaluru's 110-bed Suguna Hospital
body: Fortis Healthcare has bought Suguna Hospital on Dr Rajkumar Road in Rajajinagar, north-west Bengaluru, in an all-cash deal.
The 110-bed hospital, opened in 2006, can grow to about 150 beds; Fortis gets the land and building too.
It fits Fortis's plan to grow in city clusters by buying hospitals.
stories.joke: Bengaluru's newest Fortis branch comes with a pre-installed neighbourhood.
stories.vc: Buying running hospitals is faster and cheaper than building new ones, which is why chains are on an acquisition spree.

stories.headline: Max Healthcare grows to 5,518 beds as profit rises 10%
body: Max Healthcare's gross revenue rose 20% to ₹3,219 crore in the September quarter, and profit grew 10% to ₹448 crore.
It now runs 5,518 beds, 758 more than a year ago, with 77% occupancy.
Average revenue per patient rose 8% to ₹2.31 lakh.
stories.joke: Business is booming. Ideally, that's not a sign you should be happy about.
stories.vc: Bed additions plus rising revenue per patient is the growth formula investors pay for in Indian hospital stocks.

stories.headline: Delhi's RML Hospital clears a big hurdle for its 666-bed block
body: The new 666-bed super speciality block at Delhi's Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital has got fire safety clearance.
Built for ₹482 crore, it has 18 operating theatres, 99 ICU beds and cancer treatment machines.
It will raise the hospital's capacity from 1,538 to 2,204 beds.
stories.vc: Big public hospital expansions keep advanced care affordable and set the price benchmark private chains compete against.
